newsitem.title: USA: Empi backs analysts' 1996 EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: Empi backs analysts' 1996 EPS estimates.

text.p: Empi Inc President Joseph Laptewicz said he is comfortable with First Call analyst earnings estimates of $0.26 a share for the third quarter and $1.04 for 1996.
Asked about estimates, Laptewicz said, "We're comfortable with analysts' expectations."
"Our objective is to grow (net income) at 15 to 20 percent. We're at 21 percent year to date, so I think we'll be within that 15 to 20 percent window for the year," he said.
The $1.04 a share mean estimate for 1996 would be a 16 percent increase from the $0.90 that Empi made in 1995.

Laptewicz told a Dain Bosworth conference that Empi hopes to improve its revenue growth. He added that while Empi, which makes a variety of medical devices, has shown only three to four percent revenue growth, the target is 10 to 15 percent growth "over the long haul."
He also said Empi hopes to secure a favorable coverage determination from Medicare on its Innova PFS product, a female incontinence device.
In May, Empi said it was advised that Medicare would not reimburse costs for the PFS product.
"We're hopeful that we can move to a favorable (Medicare coverage) decision sometime in 1997," Laptewicz sid.
He told Reuters that Empi's research and development expenses, which declined in the first half, will rise in the second to reach 1995 levels of $3.4 million.
